name: Venlafaxine
route_note: Oral immediate-release tablets two to three times daily or extended-release capsules/tablets once daily.

discovery.note: A phenethylamine bicyclic derivative developed at Wyeth in the 1980s as a dual reuptake inhibitor without tricyclic receptor effects.

tagline: The first widely used SNRI, with dose-dependent noradrenergic effects
summary: Venlafaxine is a serotonin–noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor used for depression and anxiety disorders. At low doses it acts mainly on serotonin reuptake, adding noradrenaline reuptake inhibition at higher doses. Its main active metabolite, desvenlafaxine, is marketed separately.
mechanism: Venlafaxine and its active metabolite O-desmethylvenlafaxine inhibit reuptake of serotonin and, more weakly, noradrenaline; dopamine reuptake is inhibited only slightly. Serotonergic effects predominate at lower doses, with noradrenergic effects contributing at higher doses, which can raise blood pressure.
It has little affinity for muscarinic, histaminergic or alpha-adrenergic receptors, distinguishing it from tricyclic antidepressants.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Effexor for depression.

history.title: Extended release
history.detail: Effexor XR once-daily capsules are approved.

history.title: GAD
history.detail: Effexor XR becomes approved for generalised anxiety disorder.

history.title: Suicidality warning
history.detail: Class boxed warning on antidepressant suicidality in young people.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic immediate-release venlafaxine is available; XR generics follow in 2010.

history.title: Desvenlafaxine
history.detail: Its metabolite desvenlafaxine is approved as Pristiq.

safety.boxed_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours in children, adolescents and young adults (under 25) taking antidepressants; monitor for clinical worsening.

facts: Venlafaxine is more toxic in overdose than SSRIs, though less than tricyclics.
